web_true_now_not_modelled: Deferred reciprocal management fees (18-month deferral) now flowing through, aiding 2026-2027 margins beyond RWP growth; policy-fee economics on a compounding renewal base; Reciprocal holds 16.2M PRCH shares as non-admitted capital; June 2026 share sale to Porch captive at $7.17; $100M cat bond placed top of tower (2026-07-29 8-K; 2026-06-23 artemis.bm).
web_demand_product: Homeowners insurance: legacy Homeowners of America policy plus the newer Porch Insurance product, sold via independent insurance agencies and fed by home-inspection and title software plus moving services. web_price_volume_mix: Volume-led. Reciprocal Policies Written 58.7k, +38% YoY; RWP per Policy Written fell 16% YoY to $2,383 from $2,843 and premium per new customer fell 4% YoY, reflecting a softer market with competitors cutting prices (2026-07-29 8-K). Pricing ran slightly below plan.
web_bottleneck: Porch's own constraint is distribution and conversion execution plus state filing speed, not capital: statutory surplus of $169.9M supports over $800M of premium (2026-07-29 8-K). The bottleneck it relieves is scarce, well-priced homeowners capacity, advantaged by proprietary data for lower loss ratios.
web_who_benefits_next: Reinsurance and cat-bond investors (inaugural $100M Harbor Crest Re 2026-1, 2026-06-23 artemis.bm); independent insurance agencies earning commissions on 148% more branch locations; Porch's captive reinsurer buying PRCH shares at $7.17 (2026-07-29 8-K); title and inspection software partners.
web_who_loses: Incumbent homeowners carriers and their agency distribution in Texas and expansion states, losing share and forced to cut prices as Porch writes more policies at lower loss ratios; Porch concedes competitors lowered pricing in May 2026, pressuring conversion (2026-07-29 8-K and call).
web_margin_collapse_risk: A severe catastrophe year eroding Reciprocal statutory surplus below the roughly 5-to-1 RWP-to-surplus guardrail (surplus $169.9M), spiking reinsurance costs, or price competition compressing the take rate below its recent 60-65% band (2026-07-29 8-K and call).
web_low_cost_substitute: Not found. No Chinese or other low-cost substitute for US homeowners insurance identified. The nearest substitute is cheaper policies from incumbent carriers, whose price cuts stepped down Porch conversion in May 2026 before Porch responded with targeted pricing (2026-07-29 call, aggregator).
web_ceo_promised: Ehrlichman, 2026-07-29 (8-K and call): positive net income attributable to Porch for full-year 2026, 2027 and beyond; more than 70,000 Reciprocal policies written per quarter by year-end; FY26 Adjusted EBITDA $119-125M; leverage below 3x this year; $600M FY26 Reciprocal Written Premium target.
web_did_they_deliver: Yes. Q2 2026 (2026-07-29 8-K) delivered net income attributable to Porch $5.6M, Adjusted EBITDA excluding Reciprocal $39.1M up 150% YoY, policies written +38% YoY versus +33% in Q1, and Porch raised FY26 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $119-125M from prior $103-109M and revenue to $506-517M from $495-507M.
web_what_would_falsify: Q3 2026 results (estimated 2026-11-04, nasdaq.com) showing Reciprocal statutory surplus below $169.9M, Reciprocal policies written growth decelerating below 38% YoY or missing the more-than-70,000-per-quarter year-end ramp, or Insurance Services take rate falling below roughly 60% (2026-07-29 8-K and call).
